verdicts.opus: B and D both reproduced the measured rise to the 2022 peak and the decline to 776, along with the flat no-change projection and its widening bounds. B went further: it charted the central scenario, exported the scenario rows, and used a pre-pandemic baseline. It also explained why naive linear extrapolation fails (worse MAE, and no-change over-predicting a falling series), which is exactly the trap this question sets. A honestly declined to answer, while C offered memory estimates on a different scale with an internally inconsistent range.
verdicts.gpt: D is the strongest decision aid: it traces the full observed series, gives the three-year central path and sensitivity bounds, compares periods on one scale, and states the limits and follow-up calls. C is careful and largely accurate but omits the forecast bounds from its chart and lacks a second export; D loses ground by overstating coverage and framing a mature plateau as a stronger conclusion than the series alone warrants.
